questions.q: What protocol/service does PowerShell Remoting actually run on?
options: WinRM (Windows Remote Management), listening on port 5985 (HTTP) or 5986 (HTTPS)
The SQL Server Browser service
RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol)
FTP on port 21
questions.explain: PowerShell Remoting is built on WinRM, Microsoft's WS-Management implementation, not RDP or any SQL-specific service.

options: Starts the WinRM service, creates a listener, and opens the firewall rule on the target machine
Installs the dbatools module
Creates a new SQL Server login
Enables xp_cmdshell on a SQL instance
questions.explain: It's a one-time setup step (often handled via Group Policy in a domain) for the remoting transport itself, unrelated to SQL Server configuration.

questions.q: Inside an Invoke-Command script block targeting SQLPRD01, why is -SqlInstance localhost correct rather than a mistake?
options: The script block executes on the remote machine itself, so from that machine's own point of view the SQL instance is local
localhost is a required dbatools keyword with no real meaning
It's actually a bug that happens to work
Invoke-Command automatically renames every server to localhost
questions.explain: Invoke-Command runs the code ON the target server, so referencing the SQL instance as localhost from inside that block is accurate, not accidental.

questions.q: Why use New-PSSession instead of repeated Invoke-Command -ComputerName calls?
options: New-PSSession keeps a persistent connection open, avoiding reconnection and authentication overhead across multiple commands
New-PSSession is required before dbatools will load
There is no difference between the two
New-PSSession only works on Linux targets
questions.explain: Invoke-Command -ComputerName opens and tears down a connection each call; New-PSSession keeps one open for reuse, which matters when running several commands against the same servers.

questions.q: What is the key difference between PowerShell Remoting and a direct dbatools call like Get-DbaDatabase -SqlInstance SQLPRD01?
options: Remoting runs code ON a remote machine over WinRM; a direct dbatools call runs from wherever you are and talks to SQL Server over the network, no remoting involved
They are exactly the same thing under a different name
dbatools calls always require Invoke-Command internally
PowerShell Remoting only works with Oracle databases
questions.explain: Confusing these two is common — remoting is about where code executes, while a plain dbatools call is just a network connection to a SQL Server instance.
